dedupe_keys.name: san francisco lifelines council interdependency study 2014 earthquake recovery of lifeline services

description: This case study describes the 2014 interdependency study of San Francisco's Lifelines Council, which examined how dependencies among lifeline systems would affect restoration after a major earthquake. The council was formed by the City of San Francisco in 2009, after a SPUR report on lifeline resilience, and brings together more than 30 public and private service providers and city offices; CISA presents the case in its Infrastructure Dependency Primer. Because providers would not share proprietary quantitative data, the study used structured interviews with 11 lifeline service providers about response, restoration and dependencies. It identified geographic and infrastructure choke points and gaps in coordinated planning and mitigation, and led to a five-year plan with tabletop exercises and later studies of flooding and sea level rise. Coverage is the City and County of San Francisco. Format and access: a CISA web page summarising the study. Licence: US government page, no licence stated; free. Caveats: findings are qualitative and the underlying report was not read. It is a model for eliciting dependency data when operators will not share models. Related catalogue records are the Argonne dependency analysis report and the UNDRR GAR 2019 interdependency analysis paper.
